title: A Sandbagging Red-Teaming Dataset with Human-Annotated Difficulty Tiers

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: a calibrated difficulty-labeled dataset enables controlled sandbagging experiments, but the impact is indirect as it enables others' research rather than producing safety findings directly.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: curating 200 questions from existing benchmarks and adding difficulty labels is accessible. Running sandbagging prompts and measuring performance requires only basic prompt engineering.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: 200 questions, difficulty annotations, instructed sandbagging runs, baseline results. The scope is well-defined and achievable within 30 hours.

evidence: Sandbagging research exists (AISI frontier trends report, International AI Safety Report 2026), but focuses on detection methods rather than providing a curated dataset with human-annotated difficulty tiers.
Red-teaming difficulty stratification exists in cybersecurity evaluations (Task Difficulty Level framework) but has not been applied specifically to sandbagging scenarios.
Existing benchmarks lack a purpose-built dataset with calibrated difficulty labels designed specifically for controlled sandbagging experiments.
The combination of human-annotated difficulty tiers + sandbagging-specific red-teaming dataset is a distinct contribution not found in current literature.
